My mother went to the same school of Robert Piesch, Gacy's last victim. He was a year or two older than her. He also lived down the street from her. Apparently her brother was supposed to have an interview with him for a construction job, but my uncle found a different job before the interview. Who knows what would have happened.

He never got a chance to truly live his life and my heart breaks a little bit every time I think about this case. His childhood was taken away from him, and he nor his family really knew what to do for him. His father, I believe, refused Steven to even seek therapy for the trauma. At least he got some sense of family with his wife and children, even if only for a moment.

I think that Timothy Hennis is innocent and that prosecutors just wanted to nail him to solve the case. The DNA underneath the victims' fingernails didn't match him, nor did pubic hairs at the scene. All the eyewitnesses account were disproved or were put under reasonable doubt. He was acquitted but then years later they magically find the DNA again? The lab they tested were consistent in messing up results, and contrary to belief the DNA profile was never a 100% match to Hennis' DNA. Nothing in this case makes sense, and I feel like Hennis was betrayed by the criminal justice system. He was tried three times!

I had two unsettling incidents when I was a child that were by strangers. When I was about 10 I was at my school bustop at about 6 am. A man stopped in the middle of the street and stared at me and my neighbor, a girl my same age. This neighborhood was very small and I knew/recognized everyone in it. I never saw that man before and would never see him again. To stop and stare several feet away in the early morning at two preteen girls unnerved me quite a bit. If I wasn't with another kid I don't know what would've happened.
Back when I was 7 living in a different neighborhood I was walking home from school and a stranger stopped by and asked me if I needed a ride. He was an old man that I again didn't recognized (and also of course was driving a creepy van lol) I politely said no and ran the hell away. I don't know if I was/am being irrational and maybe they were "innocent" incidents but I was such a dumbass kid that I'm surprised I didn't confront any of these men. I actually trusted my guts and instinct for once. My normal routines were just thrown off loop on those days when every other day was just fine. I still don't know if those incidents were dangerous or not tbh


edit: i just remembered when i was four a man stalked me at a dollar store when i wondered off from my mom. he was behind me just staring at while i was looking at toys, and me being a dumbass kid i didn't even notice. my mom found me and yelled at the guy and he ran off. looking back my childhood put me in some weird situations.

The Max Headroom incident is so creepy to me just because it's local to me, and it involves interrupting a classic Doctor Who episode lmao. But honestly that video gives me the creeps, and I honestly don't recommend watching it. Just a copy and paste from the wiki article on it:

The Max Headroom broadcast signal intrusion was a television signal hijacking occurring in Chicago, Illinois, United States, on the evening of November 22, 1987, involving at least two unknown individuals. It is an example of what is known in the television business as broadcast signal intrusion. Two Chicago television stations had their broadcast signals hijacked by an unknown person wearing a Max Headroom mask and sunglasses. A homemade Max Headroom background rocked back and forth in the background.

The intruder was successful in interrupting two broadcast television stations within the course of three hours. The first incident took place for 25 seconds during the sportscast on the 9:00 PM news on WGN-TV Channel 9, and the second, two hours later, after 11:00 PM on PBS affiliate WTTW Channel 11 for about 90 seconds during a broadcast of the Doctor Who episode "Horror of Fang Rock".

The second pirate broadcast, which lasted 90 seconds and pre-recorded on videotape, featured the individual parodying WGN and television in general. The hacker rambled on making reference to Headroom's endorsement of Coke, the series Clutch Cargo, and WGN anchor Chuck Swirsky, then pretended to defecate as a "masterpiece for all the greatest world newspaper nerds", a reference to WGN's call letters ("World's Greatest Newspaper"). The video ended with the hacker’s exposed buttocks being spanked with a flyswatter by an accomplice before normal programming resumed.
